prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Lange deutsche Komposita (language de).
Grid: 3 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Begriff" · longest unbreakable word 546px · one-line width 546px
  col 2: header "Kurzform" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 101px
  col 3: header "Erklärung" · longest unbreakable word 186px · one-line width 1091px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A glossary of very long German compounds: each row pairs an identifier-like headword (Begriff) with a short abbreviation (Kurzform) and a prose explanation (Erklärung). The reader looks up a term, checks its short form, then reads the explanation — so the table is scanned row by row, not column by column, and the headword is the anchor that must remain recognisable.","reading":"Vertical scan down column 1 to find the term, a quick glance at column 2 (a lookup key, not read as text), then a horizontal read of column 3 as running prose. Because col 1 entries are 300–546px unbreakable strings, at 360px they will break mid-word no matter what; the real choice is how much of that damage to absorb versus how much readable measure to give the prose and how much horizontal scrolling to impose.","groups":["col 1 (Begriff) and col 2 (Kurzform) form one unit — the term and its label, read together as the row's identity; they should sit adjacent and tight.","col 3 (Erklärung) is a separate register: continuous prose that only needs a workable measure, and it benefits from a clear gap after the identifier pair."],"keep_intact":["Kurzform values — short abbreviations (≤83px); splitting them destroys their meaning, so this column must never go below ~104px.","Begriff headwords ideally whole (546px worst case), which is only possible with a wide column / horizontal scroll.","Hyphenated compounds such as 'Kraftfahrzeug-Haftpflichtversicherung' should break at the hyphen, not mid-morpheme."],"may_wrap":["Erklärung — multi-clause prose (one-line 1091px); it wraps naturally and its row height can absorb 2–5 lines without harming the row's unity.","The longest Begriff strings, if the column is kept narrow; each row already has spare vertical height, so 2–3 line headwords remain scannable."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [120, 104, 135] · table 360×1673px · row heights [36, 269, 246, 315, 315, 222, 269] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 13 lines · mid-word splits 13
Design r0B: widths [175, 104, 80] · table 360×2905px · row heights [60, 501, 455, 548, 525, 362, 455] · column headers wrapped 1/3 · tallest cell 23 lines · mid-word splits 51
Design r0C: widths [567, 104, 400] · table 1072×534px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 106, 83, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 712px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r0A","good":"Fits entirely inside the 360px box, so the reader never scrolls and each row is a self-contained unit on one screen; the Kurzform column (104px) stays intact and legible, and the identifier pair sits adjacent as intended. Row order and rhythm are readable — you can see the whole glossary in one vertical sweep.","problems":"Both of the wide columns are destroyed. The headwords break into arbitrary 7–9 character shards ('Donauampf / schifffahrtsg / esellschaft'), which makes the anchor term unrecognisable — the one thing the reader came to look up. Worse, the Erklärung breaks mid-word in every line ('Gesellschaftsfor / m der / Personenschiff / ahrt'), so the prose is unreadable as prose: 13 mid-word splits and a 13-line tallest cell. Row heights balloon to 222–315px, and the table becomes 1673px tall, so 'one glance per row' becomes a scroll of its own.","cause":"The 359px budget is split three ways: col 3 gets only 135px → 114px of text (about 15 characters per line), while col 1 gets 120px → 99px of text for strings that need 300–546px. The table is 2905px tall — a single row (501–548px) is taller than the phone screen, so a row can no longer be read as a unit at all. It is the honest floor: if you insist on staying near 360px, this is the least damaging allocation, but it cannot fix the fundamental mismatch."}]}
